title: 4.10 I start work at half past eight
unit_title: Life at home, every day and yesterday
unit_outcome: Say where people and things are at home, talk about the lights and machines, ask what there is, describe someone's morning in order, say what you did yesterday and on which day, ask and tell the time, say how often you do things and give dates.
lesson_title: I start work at half past eight
sub_lesson_title: I start work at half past eight
goal: Ask and say when people start and finish work, with half past and o'clock (What time do you start work? I start work at half past eight.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 4.10 What Time Is It?: A1 reads whole hours; A1+ 4.10 adds half past (half past eight) and asks about the workday with What time do you…? (What time do you start work? I start work at half past nine.). It is the only Unit 4 lesson with clock times, after the user's 2026-10-31 note that A1+ drilled clock time too much; the times hang on start work and finish work. The stated time is shown by the shared teaching clock, never by a photograph: A1+ 1.1's reviewed workday photos of Ana and Luis show no clock. Picture banks change only the person, never the time, and keep each person's start and finish (and leave and arrive) photos apart because they are close scenes; Listen sets half past against o'clock.
prerequisite: A1 4.10 What time is it? / o'clock; A1+ 1.2 he/she -s; A1 6.12 What time does … leave?
speaking_outcome: Say half past as one group (HAF-past) before the hour; start and finish keep their final sounds. Do not require native-like speed.
